What is the OS version and build number of the affected device?

Is there any signing error when using biometric features like fingerprint or face recognition?

IsUserAzureAD: NO
This indicates the user failed to pass Azure Active Directory (AAD) authentication during the logon process and did not get the Azure AD Primary Refresh Token (PRT). Please check if the user can sign in to Azure Portal from the device successfully.
Collect the following event logs during the logon process to check why the authentication against AAD failed:
Event Viewer -> Applications and Services -> Microsoft -> Windows -> AAD -> Operational
Event Viewer -> Applications and Services -> Microsoft -> Windows -> AAD -> Analytic

If Azureprt is missing engage AzureAD team to check the AAD logs for the user and device to see why the PRT was not issued. Engage AAD team to check the AAD logs for the user and device to see why the Enterprise PRT was not issued.
l2:
AADJ cloud-only join scenarios
When you join a Windows 10/11 device to AAD (cloud-only join), the user will be prompted to enroll WHFB. This is a Windows 10/11 OS default.
Some customers ask how to disable this. It is recommended to manage these non-domain joined systems with Intune. This feature can be managed and disabled by Intune or registry keys.
Use Intune to disable Windows Hello for Business enrollment
User Policy
HKEY_USERS\UserSID\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\PassportForWork
Device Policy
HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\PassportForWork
DWORD "Enabled"
Value = 0 for Disable and Value = 1 for Enable

AdfsRefreshToken: NO
This indicates the user failed to get authenticated with Active Directory Federation Services (ADFS) and did not get the Enterprise PRT.
Collect data using auth script and validate Confirm they have Server 2016/2019/2022 domain controllers with certificates intended for Kerberos Authentication and Smart card logon

Check KDC event logs and validate If a suitable certificate is found by the KDC service, an event ID 302 (Kerberos-Key-Distribution-Center) will be logged, detailing the issuer name, serial number, thumbprint, and certificate template.
If no suitable certificate is found by the KDC service, an event ID 200 (Kerberos-Key-Distribution-Center) will be logged to notify that the KDC could not find a suitable certificate to use.
The issuing CA of the KDC certificate must be present in the computer NTAuth store, both on the Domain Controller (DC) and on the WHFB client device.

l1: Collect Windows Hello for Business event logs from Event Viewer -> Applications and Services -> Microsoft -> Windows -> HelloForBusiness.
Collect User Device Registration event logs from Event Viewer -> Applications and Services -> Microsoft -> Windows -> User Device Registration.
Run 'dsregcmd /status' and capture the output to check device registration state.
Collect ng_trace.zip if available for comprehensive authentication tracing.
Run the Microsoft WHFB diagnostic collection script if available in the environment.
l2: Collect Kerberos.etl trace to analyze error codes received from the Domain Controller or authentication point, including which identity was authenticating and what SPN or URL was being accessed.
Collect KDC.etl from the Domain Controller when the KDC service is returning errors to understand why the KDC failed to find a SPN or route a UPN.
Collect Hfb_Oper.evtx which contains detailed information about Windows Hello for Business provisioning processes.
Export NgcPolicyGp-key.txt and NgcPolicyGpUser-key.txt to capture the Group Policy settings applied to devices related to WHFB configuration.

steps.expect: Check if 'IsUserAzureAD' shows NO, indicating PRT was not issued

steps.action: Verify user can sign in to Azure Portal from the device
steps.expect: If sign-in fails, the issue is with Azure AD authentication, not WHFB specifically
